newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon inaugurates new offshore oil platform.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon inaugurates new offshore oil platform.

text.p: Cameroon has inaugurated a new offshore oil platform with a capacity to produce 10,000 barrels per day of crude for export from the Ebome field off the southern tourist resort of Kribi.

"With the capacity to produce 10,000 barrels of crude oil per day this Ebome platform is the 10th petroleum production centre in the country," President Paul Biya said at an inauguration ceremony on Friday.
The Ebome field, which has three functional wells, came on stream on January 12. Officals said the first crude from the field would be lifted by the end of February.

A consortium composed of Kelt, a subsidiary of French company PERINCO, Mobil Corp and the Cameroon National Hydrocarbon Corporation SNH is behind the Ebome project which Biya said had cost an estimated $30 million.

French company Elf Aquitaine established a commercial oilfield near the border with Nigeria in 1976. After peaking at just over nine million tonnes (over 66 million barrels a year or 180,000 bpd) in 1985, Cameroon's production has declined steadily.
Biya said Cameroon remained "a modest oil producer" but said studies were underway in four other sectors -- three around Kribi and one in an area he identified as Moundi.
Biya said potential reserves of natural gas estimated at 100 billion cubic metres had been identified in the Douala, Kribi and Campo areas and that studies would begin there shortly.

In the past, Cameroon's government has been reluctant to reveal oil production figures and does not include receipts from oil exports in budget estimates -- a sore point with the International Monetary Fund.
The IMF has linked a deal on three-year medium-term financing to oil export proceeds being included in the budget.
